Small employers are not expected to use elaborate scoring matrices; a fair and honest selection process within the band of reasonable responses can suffice, but selection based on a manager's unstructured impression of who is "weaker" is subjective, without objective criteria, consultation, or any fair basis. Tribunals have held that even small employers must apply fair, objective criteria and consult with the employee; the lack of any criteria and reliance on a bare impression generally falls outside the band of reasonable responses (Mitchells of Lancaster v Gibson and similar cases).
